scope: Qualitative visual review of three user-uploaded memory-probe preview TIFFs. No model inference.
coordinateMeaning: Bounding boxes from differing RGB pixels against normal panel, excluding 40-pixel header, per 1024-square panel. They locate overlays, not annotated subject boundaries.

frames.retainedBank: Overlay on rubble at the top/left edge of the pile behind the bucket. Qualitative false-positive mask, not visible worker segmentation.

frames.conditioningOnly: Overlay on a pale rubble patch to the right of the orange marker, away from the intended worker. Qualitative false-positive mask.

frames.normalGPU: empty despite visible worker upper body
frames.conditioningOnly: Highlights the intended worker's visible upper body below the raised bucket.
frames.retainedBank: Highlights the intended worker's visible upper body below the raised bucket.

conclusions: Both memory probes can reacquire the visible worker at the reviewed return frame without a new tap.
Each probe also produces a visually incorrect rubble mask at one of the earlier reviewed frames. Nonempty masks cannot by themselves authorize recovery or memory updates.
Identical overlay bounding boxes at 175 do not imply pixel-identical masks. This is three-frame qualitative evidence, not a complete sequence annotation.
Report states experimental outputs never enter history and frozen slots retain capture-time age semantics. This is not validation of an online recovery policy.

Next proposed diagnostic should evaluate recovery acceptance and subsequent tracking with feedback, while preserving time advancement and checking false positives. Confidence or consecutive-frame heuristics require independent validation and do not guarantee identity.
